title: AI Lead Scoring Engine
tagline: Prioritize prospects based on fit, pain signals, and buying intent.
businessOutcomes: Your team works the most promising leads first.
summary: Scores leads based on industry fit, location, business size, review signals, website quality, CRM history, engagement, and likely need.
businessProblem: Sales teams treat every lead equally — reps spend time on poor-fit prospects while high-intent accounts sit in the queue because there's no consistent scoring model beyond gut feel.
outcome: Every lead and account carries a transparent score (0–100) with factor breakdown — reps work the highest-scored untouched leads first and marketing sees which segments convert.
expectedOutcomes: Every lead and account carries a transparent score (0–100) with factor breakdown — reps work the highest-scored untouched leads first and marketing sees which segments convert.
whoItsFor: B2B teams with 50+ leads per month where prioritization matters — agencies, SaaS, and professional services with defined ICPs.
aiInputs: ICP fit criteria: industry, geography, size proxies
Review sentiment and rating from public listings
Website quality signals (SSL, mobile, content freshness)
CRM engagement history: emails opened, meetings booked, form fills
Pain signal tags from lead finder or research workflows
aiOutputs: Composite lead score (0–100) with weighted factor breakdown
Tier label: Hot / Warm / Cold / Disqualified
Top 3 reasons for score with evidence citations
CRM field update payload for score and tier
noCodeTools: HubSpot lead scoring rules + ChatGPT enrichment columns in Sheets
Clay.com scoring table combining Places, reviews, and CRM lookup
Zapier: new lead → GPT score → HubSpot property update
lowCodeTools: n8n nightly: pull new leads → enrich → OpenAI score → CRM update
Google Sheets model with weighted factors + Apps Script CRM sync
Make.com with Salesforce Flow for score-triggered task creation
customBuildStack: Scoring engine with configurable weights per ICP factor
OpenAI for qualitative website and review analysis
HubSpot/Salesforce custom properties for score storage
Dashboard showing score distribution and conversion correlation
implementationSteps: Define scoring factors and weights aligned to your ICP — document in a rubric
Connect CRM and public data sources for enrichment fields
Build baseline rule-based score first; add AI qualitative layer second
Backtest scores against last 6 months won/lost deals — adjust weights
Set CRM automation: Hot leads → instant task; Cold → nurture sequence
Review score-to-close correlation monthly and recalibrate
systemBehavior: Recalculates on new lead creation and weekly for existing pipeline
Transparent factor breakdown — not a black-box number
Does not auto-disqualify without human-defined rules
Logs score history to detect drift over time
Read-only on external sources; writes score fields to CRM only
risks: Scores trained on biased historical data perpetuate bad targeting
Over-reliance on public review data skews toward consumer-facing businesses
Reps may ignore low-score leads that are actually strategic accounts
Frequent weight changes without communication erode team trust
